record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: What is the origin of dark matter, and can off-shell particles arising from causal-set-inspired nonlocal scalar quantum field theory provide a viable dark matter candidate, including a production mechanism in early-universe dense and hot conditions and potentially observable signatures despite zero non-gravitational scattering involving off-shell particles?

evidence.quote: The origin of dark matter, the mysterious dominant mass density in our universe, is a major open question in cosmology.
They found a set of on-shell and off-shell solutions in the mode expansion of the quantized field operator. These off-shell particles do not satisfy the conventional dispersion relation.
In other words, any scattering with off-shell particles has zero cross-section. This prompted them to consider these off-shell particles as a natural candidate for dark matter.
Specifically, post-inflation reheating and radiation self-interaction provide the dense and hot conditions that lead to efficient relevant scattering processes.
Despite this detection challenge, in Refs. 32 and 33 some potentially observable signatures of this model are suggested.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a real scalar quantum field theory on Minkowski spacetime whose kinetic operator is a nonlocal, retarded, Lorentz-invariant operator B obtained as a continuum limit of a discrete d'Alembertian defined on causal sets (sprinklings of spacetime points with the induced causal order). The mode expansion of the quantized field operator associated with B contains, in addition to the usual on-shell modes satisfying the standard relativistic dispersion relation p^2 = m^2, a continuous family of "off-shell" modes whose four-momenta do not lie on any mass shell. Suppose interactions are introduced so that on-shell quanta can scatter to produce off-shell quanta, while any scattering amplitude with an off-shell particle in the initial or final state vanishes (zero non-gravitational cross-section for off-shell quanta).

(a) Determine whether such off-shell quanta can constitute a viable candidate for the cosmological dark matter, i.e., reproduce the observed relic abundance Ω_DM h^2 ≈ 0.12 and be consistent with cosmological and astrophysical constraints (structure formation, CMB, etc.).

(b) Construct an explicit production mechanism for these off-shell quanta in the early universe, taking into account the dense and hot conditions following post-inflationary reheating and radiation self-interaction, and compute the resulting relic abundance as a function of the nonlocality scale, the inflationary reheating temperature, and the couplings of the underlying scalar theory.

(c) Identify any potentially observable signatures (gravitational, cosmological, or otherwise) that could distinguish this off-shell dark matter scenario from alternative dark matter candidates, despite the assumed vanishing of all non-gravitational scattering involving off-shell particles.
artifact.category_tag: causal set theory and dark matter
artifact.status_search_result: The proposal of off-shell quanta from causal-set-inspired nonlocal scalar QFT as a dark matter candidate has been explored in works such as "Dark matter from spacetime nonlocality" (Phys. Rev. D 92, 103504, 2015) and "Off-shell Dark Matter: A Cosmological relic of Quantum Gravity" (Phys. Rev. D 95, 043514, 2017), which sketch a production mechanism and connect the reheating temperature to inflaton parameters. However, a complete derivation of the relic abundance, a verified production model consistent with all cosmological constraints, and concrete observational signatures remain unresolved. The origin of dark matter is itself an outstanding open problem in cosmology, so the question is open.

status_evidence.title: Dark matter from spacetime nonlocality
status_evidence.snippet: Modifying the evolution equation of a massless scalar field results in a continuum of massive particles in addition to massless ones; the massive/off-shell quanta can be produced and then no longer interact, making them a natural dark matter candidate.
status_evidence.claim: Off-shell modes from causal-set-inspired nonlocal scalar QFT are proposed as a dark matter candidate, but the relic abundance and signatures are not fully established.

status_evidence.title: Off-shell Dark Matter: A Cosmological relic of Quantum Gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Production rate suppressed by the nonlocality scale; off-shell quanta produced in early universe and effectively decouple thereafter except gravitationally.
status_evidence.claim: A production mechanism in the early universe has been outlined, with the rate suppressed by the nonlocality scale, but a viable, fully consistent dark matter scenario with observational signatures has not been established.
